name: Macrodactyly of toes, unilateral
aliases: Localized macrodactyly of a single foot

criteria.description: Unilateral enlargement of one or more toes involving soft tissue and bone
Progressive disproportionate growth of affected toes relative to contralateral side
Radiologic evidence of hypertrophy of phalanges and soft tissues in affected toes
No evidence of associated syndromic or systemic disorders causing digit enlargement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: unilateral enlargement, progressive disproportionate growth, and radiologic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral disproportionate enlargement of one or more toes
searchTerms: uneven toe size on one foot

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypertrophy of soft tissues and phalanges in affected toes
searchTerms: swollen soft tissue and bones in toes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive increase in size of affected toes from birth or early infancy

common.symptomName: Toe deformity causing functional impairment or gait disturbance
Localized soft tissue overgrowth with skin thickening
searchTerms: soft tissue overgrowth with skin thickening

common.symptomName: Asymmetry between affected and unaffected foot
Pain or discomfort due to mechanical stress on affected toes

occasional.symptomName: Secondary callus formation on plantar surface of enlarged toes
searchTerms: calluses on bottom of big toes
thick skin on sole under enlarged toes

occasional.symptomName: Nerve compression symptoms such as paresthesia in affected toes
Mild limb length discrepancy on affected side

rare.symptomName: Ulceration or skin breakdown over enlarged toes
Secondary infection of affected soft tissues
Associated vascular malformations in affected foot

imaging: X-ray showing hypertrophy of phalanges and soft tissues of affected toes
MRI demonstrating soft tissue overgrowth and exclusion of vascular malformations
other: Clinical observation of progressive unilateral toe enlargement from birth or early infancy

distinguishingFeatures: Asymmetric overgrowth involving multiple body regions
Presence of connective tissue nevi and vascular malformations
Limb hypertrophy usually involving entire limb, not isolated toes

redFlags: Rapid progression of toe enlargement beyond early childhood
Signs of vascular malformation or bleeding in affected foot
Ulceration or infection of affected soft tissues
references: Orphanet: Macrodactyly of toes, unilateral - ORPHA:295243
